sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever tried to calculate something huge—like the number of atoms in the universe—and Java just gave up? Let’s fix that!

• How to handle numbers bigger than `long` can hold
• Why `BigInteger` and `BigDecimal` are your new best friends
• When to use them (and when to stick with `int`/`double`)

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you’re counting grains of sand on a beach. A regular calculator (like `int` or `double`) would run out of digits fast—just like you’d run out of fingers!

`BigInteger` and `BigDecimal` are like super-powered calculators that never run out of space. They handle:

• **`BigInteger`**: Whole numbers of *any* size (even 1000 digits long!)
  - Perfect for cryptography, factorials, or counting stars

• **`BigDecimal`**: Precise decimal numbers (no more `0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004` nonsense!)
  - Essential for money, scientific calculations, or exact measurements

**Why not just use `double`?**
- `double` is like a rubber ruler—it stretches but loses accuracy
- `BigDecimal` is like a metal ruler—precise but slower (trade-off!)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: BigInteger handles integers of arbitrary size beyond the range of long
BigDecimal provides arbitrary-precision decimal arithmetic without rounding errors
Arithmetic uses methods: add(), subtract(), multiply(), divide() instead of operators
BigDecimal is essential for financial calculations where precision is critical
Specify a rounding mode and scale when dividing with BigDecimal

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: `BigInteger` = Unlimited-size whole numbers (no overflow!) `BigDecimal` = Precise decimals (no floating-point errors!) Use them for money, science, or huge numbers—otherwise, stick to `int`/`double`. Ready to tackle real-world math problems without limits.
